title: SANA-Video 2.0: Softmax Where It Counts
hook: Pure linear attention is cheap but loses full-rank token mixing. SANA-Video 2.0 sprinkles softmax anchors back in at a 3:1 ratio and reaches softmax-level video quality at linear-attention cost.
key_points: A hybrid video diffusion transformer at 5B and 14B scales, generating up to 720p on a single GPU.
Hybrid Linear-Softmax Attention: gated linear attention for O(N) mixing plus periodic gated-softmax anchors at a 3:1 ratio.
Block Attention Residuals route completed block summaries into later linear layers, lifting deep-layer effective rank about 12%.
Trained from scratch as a hybrid rather than linearizing a pretrained softmax model; proxy studies pick 25% softmax as the sweet spot.
VBench 84.30 with 40-step sampling in 13.2s at 480p on one H100.
Compiled forward pass runs 3.2x faster than a matched full-softmax baseline at 720p/60s, and the gap widens with duration.
content_html: Video diffusion transformers are strangled by attention: token counts scale with resolution and duration, so a full-softmax model gets expensive fast. Linear attention fixes the scaling but gives up the full-rank token interactions that make softmax expressive. SANA-Video 2.0 takes the middle road, and trains it from scratch rather than converting a softmax model after the fact.
extra_html:
The hybrid

Most layers use gated linear attention for O(N)-dominated mixing; every fourth is a gated-softmax "anchor" that restores full-rank interactions — a 3:1 ratio the authors arrive at through reduced-resolution proxy studies identifying 25% softmax as the best quality-efficiency trade-off. To keep the anchors' refreshed representations from decaying with depth, Block Attention Residuals route completed block summaries into later linear layers, reusing anchor features and lifting deep-layer effective rank by about 12%. The result is instantiated at 5B and 14B under one unified architecture and generates up to 720p on a single GPU.

The numbers

With 40-step sampling it reports a VBench score of 84.30 in 13.2 seconds at 480p on one H100, which the authors call competitive with far larger full-softmax video DiTs. The compiled forward pass is 3.2x faster than a matched full-softmax baseline at 720p/60s, and because the saving is asymptotic rather than a constant factor, that gap expands with video duration. A further full-stack inference pass (kernel fusion, caching, sparse attention) multiplies throughput again, bringing the 5B pipeline to 13.06s for 720p/5s. Chen and colleagues, arXiv 2026.

related.title: The Seriality Gap in Video Diffusion Models
related.hook: Give a video diffusion model more denoising steps and you'd expect better predictions on chains of causal events. Instead performance keeps degrading — the steps don't add real serial computation.

related.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion (Stable Diffusion)
related.hook: Running diffusion on raw pixels is brutally expensive. Do it in a compressed latent space instead, and high-res text-to-image becomes cheap enough to run on a consumer GPU.

related.title: Flex-Forcing: One Video Diffusion Model, Two Inference Modes
related.hook: Video diffusion models used to force a choice: globally coherent but slow, or fast streaming that drifts apart. Flex-Forcing chunks time and denoising steps together so one model does both.

related.title: Veo 3
related.hook: Google's Veo 3 generates video with synchronized native audio — dialogue, sound effects, and ambient noise produced together with the picture, not dubbed on after.

flashcards.prompt: What does pure linear attention lose, and how does SANA-Video 2.0 get it back?
flashcards.back_html: It lacks full-rank token interactions. The model interleaves periodic gated-softmax anchor layers among gated-linear ones at a 3:1 ratio to restore them without paying quadratic cost throughout.

flashcards.prompt: Why does SANA-Video 2.0's speed advantage over a full-softmax baseline grow with video length?

choices.text: Most of its mixing is linear in sequence length, so the quadratic softmax cost it avoids grows faster than its own
Longer videos need fewer denoising steps, so sampling gets cheaper
The model switches off attention entirely past a length threshold

flashcards.explanation_html: Longer videos mean longer token sequences; a mostly-O(N) backbone pulls further ahead of a quadratic one, which is why the 3.2x margin at 720p/60s expands with duration.

flashcards.prompt: What do Block Attention Residuals do?
flashcards.back_html: They route completed block summaries forward into later linear layers so anchor features get reused, raising deep-layer effective rank by roughly 12%.
